newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: South African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended weak in fairly active trade on Thursday as the market tried to catch up on trade lost due to repeated breakdowns in the electronic trading system since Monday.
Dealers said industrials were weak on selling by futures players, and golds slid lower on an ailing bullion price.
The gold index slid over two percent in tandem with the softer gold price which was fixed at $372.20 per ounce in London morning trade -- its lowest level in London since April 1994.
Dealers said market weakness caught them by surprise.
"Our call was for the market to go better today. Then the gold price came under pressure, the rand weakened and bonds drifted back," one said.
Although third quarter GDP figure was slightly better-than-expected, dealers said without the contribution of the agricultural sector it would have been poor.
The Central Statistical Service said gross domestic product rose a seasonally adjust and annualised 3.2 percent in the third quarter from a revised 3.7 percent second quarter rise.
A Reuters poll of economists forecast a third quarter rise of 2.5 percent, with ideas ranging widely from 1.0 to 3.5 percent.
The opening of trade on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange was delayed by 30 minutes as the exchange reverted to its original electronic trading system, first implemented in March.
The introduction of new software over the weekend has led to trade being halted continuously over the past three days, culminating in only 27 minutes of dealing on Wednesday.
The replacement system operated smoothly throughout the day, although brokers were dissatisfied as the number of terminals they could utilise was restricted.
Futures players were present in the market and dealers said trade was volatile.
Nampak was up 65 cents to 19.75, a 3.40 percent gain but closed 35 cents weaker at 18.75, a 1.83 percent loss -- all on futures activity, a dealer said.
Dealers said the market would be difficult to call on Friday as Wall Street and U.S. metals markets were closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday.
However, with the approaching futures and unit trust close-outs in December, the market was expected to move firmer in the near-term, they said.
The overall index shed 35.3 points to 6,714.1, the industrial index lost 51 points to 8,000.4 points and the gold index was off 37 points to 1,526.7 points.
Anglo added 50 cents to 258.50 rand, SA Breweries slipped 55 cents to 68.25 rand, Absa gained 45 cents to 24.95 rand and Nampak cut 35 cents to 18.75 rand.
Freegold dropped 145 cents to 34.55 rand, Vaal Reefs lost 750 cents to 321.50 rand and Kloof was 50 cents weaker at 37.75 rand.

Near-dated industrial equity futures opened firm but quickly retraced gains as the rand and bonds weakened. Dealers said there was nervousness that the spot market trading system would fail and players were wary of taking positions.
The market, however, continued weak unimpressed by the GDP figure and weaker bullion price.
The December industrial contract was at 7,741/45 from 7,862, the gold contract was at 1,070/85 from 1,069 and the all-share contract at Wednesday's 6,231 settlement.
-- Charles Phahlane, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482 1003
